[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Kubernetes Storage: Volumes, PersistentVolumes, and PersistentVolumeClaims"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In Kubernetes, managing state and data persistence requires understanding how storage abstracts from container lifecycles. While Pods are ephemeral, applications often require data to survive Pod restarts, reschedules, or deletions."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Kubernetes Volumes"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Kubernetes Volume has a lifespan that matches the Pod that encloses it. When a Pod is deleted, the volume is also deleted. However, a volume outlives any individual containers running within the Pod, and data can be shared across containers in the same Pod."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: volume-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app-container
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: "/usr/share/nginx/html"
      name: my-volume
  volumes:
  - name: my-volume
    emptyDir: {}"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. PersistentVolumes (PV)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"A PersistentVolume (PV) is a piece of storage in the cluster that has been provisioned by an administrator or dynamically provisioned using Storage Classes. It is a resource in the cluster just like a node is a cluster resource. PVs have an independent lifecycle from any individual Pod that uses them."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: task-pv-volume
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  hostPath:
    path: "/mnt/data""},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. PersistentVolumeClaims (PVC)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"A PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is a request for storage by a user. It is similar to a Pod. Pods consume node resources and PVCs consume PV resources. PVCs can request specific size and access modes."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: task-pv-claim
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 3Gi"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Using a PVC in a Pod"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once a PVC is created and bound to an appropriate PV, a Pod can use the storage by referencing the PVC name in its volume specifications."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: pv-pod
spec:
  containers:
    - name: task-pv-container
      image: nginx
      volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: "/usr/share/nginx/html"
          name: task-pv-storage
  volumes:
    - name: task-pv-storage
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: task-pv-claim"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Best Practices"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use emptyDir for temporary scratch space that does not need to persist beyond the Pod lifecycle."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use PersistentVolumes and PersistentVolumeClaims for stateful workloads like databases where data durability is critical."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverage StorageClasses for dynamic provisioning so administrators do not need to manually pre-provision PVs."}]
